parts.text: A student is determining the resistance of a resistance wire. The circuit is shown in Fig. 2.1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Record the current I in the circuit, as shown on the ammeter in Fig. 2.2. I = ........................................................ [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student places the sliding contact C at a distance l = 20.0 cm from B. She records the potential difference V across the length l of the resistance wire. She repeats the procedure using l values of 40.0 cm, 60.0 cm, 80.0 cm and 100.0 cm. All the readings are shown in Table 2.1. Calculate, and record in Table 2.1, V l for each value of l . Complete the V l column heading. Table 2.1 l / cm V / V V l / 20.0 0.50 40.0 0.92 60.0 1.62 80.0 2.08 100.0 2.40 [3]

ms.label: 2(b)(ii)
ms.text:

V/cm

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Look carefully at the values of V l in Table 2.1.

ms.label: 2(c)
ms.text:

Values are close OR values are within the limits of experimental accuracy

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Tick the box to show your conclusion from the results. V l is approximately constant. V l is decreasing as V increases. V l is increasing as V increases. There is no simple pattern for V l in the results. [1]

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Calculate the resistance of 100 cm of the resistance wire using the equation R = V I , where V is the potential difference across 100 cm of the resistance wire. Use the value of current I from part (a) . Give your answer to a suitable number of significant figures for this experiment and include the unit. R = ........................................................ [3]
